narrative: Material PL1__MED357F1 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.62) with a confirmed upward trend across the observation window (March 2025 – March 2026). Lead times are extremely short (~0.099 working days) but moderately variable (CV=0.32), making demand variability the dominant uncertainty driver at 71.5% of total variance. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with safety stock of 473 units and reorder point of 607 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level target, while remaining well within the 2,209-unit storage constraint.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0; this provides no buffer against the observed demand variability (CV=0.62).
Upward demand trend detected — mean demand estimate may be conservative; monitor and update quarterly.
5 outliers winsorised at upper bound 3312 units.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with fixed reorder point and fixed order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Given the high daily demand volume (mean 1,355 units), erratic but largely non-intermittent pattern (95.1% non-zero days), and extremely short lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) model minimises response lag and matches the near-real-time replenishment capability implied by sub-day lead times. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs efficiently at this volume.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (2,209 units) is non-binding for the current policy (SS=473 + OQ=1,395 = 1,868 units, headroom=341 units). If the demand trend continues, safety stock requirements will rise and may eventually compress the feasible order quantity below EOQ; recommend re-evaluating capacity allocation within 12 months.
